title: Can't decide if an onboarding prompt should ask questions first or just commit to a draft
author: peanutanche
selftext:
I'm working on an worldbuilding tool and stuck on a design decision.

Here's the situation. If a player drops a one-line prompt like *"Make an original world called Aethelgard — floating isles held aloft by singing crystals, where skyfarers duel on windships"* then what should the AI do next?

I've tried two approaches.

**Version 1 asks questions before it writes anything.** Stuff like: are the crystals just a resource or do they have some kind of will? Are the duels a sport, piracy, or basically diplomacy with cannons? It feels more respectful of what the user actually wants, but it's a whole extra round trip before they see anything real.

**Version 2 commits and writes.** It gives you named characters, factions, a conflict, all in one go, then says *"tell me what to cut or twist."* Way more satisfying on first contact. But sometimes it guesses wrong and now the user is stuck arguing with a draft instead of building one.

Here's a chunk of what Version 2 spit out, so you can see what "commit to a draft" actually looks like:

>

Reads fine to me, but I can't tell if that's actually good onboarding or if it's just AI plot soup that happens to be well-organized.

Has anyone dealt with this exact fork before，like ask-first versus commit-first for a cold start? Does it change depending on whether it's someone's first session or a returning user?
